title: The Tortoise and the Hare
content:
One sunny day, a fast hare laughed at a slow tortoise.

"You are so slow!" said the hare. "I can run very fast."

"Let us have a race," said the tortoise with a smile.

All the animals came to watch. "Run, run, run!" they cheered.

The hare ran very, very fast. He was far ahead. The tortoise walked slow and small.

"I am so fast," said the hare. "I will take a little nap." He sat under a tree and closed his eyes.

The tortoise did not stop. Step by step, he walked and walked.

The hare slept and slept. The tortoise walked past him, quiet and slow.

When the hare woke up, he ran fast. But it was too late!

The tortoise was at the finish line. "I did it!" he said.

All the animals cheered for the slow, happy tortoise.

"Slow and steady wins the race," said the tortoise. And everyone smiled.

title: The Lion and the Mouse
content:
A big lion was sleeping in the warm sun.

A little mouse ran up his back. The lion woke up and caught the mouse.

"Please let me go," said the little mouse. "One day I will help you."

The lion laughed. "You are so small! How can you help me?"

But the lion was kind. He opened his big paw and let the mouse go.

"Thank you, thank you!" said the happy mouse.

One day, the lion was caught in a net. He could not get out.

"Help! Help!" cried the lion.

The little mouse heard him. She ran fast to the lion.

The mouse used her tiny teeth. She bit the net, again and again.

The net broke, and the lion was free!

"Thank you, little friend," said the lion. "You did help me."

The big lion and the little mouse were friends forever.

title: The Little Red Hen
content:
A little red hen found some seeds of wheat.

"Who will help me plant the seeds?" she asked.

"Not I," said the cat. "Not I," said the dog. "Not I," said the duck.

"Then I will do it myself," said the little red hen. And she did.

The wheat grew tall and gold. "Who will help me cut the wheat?" she asked.

"Not I," said the cat. "Not I," said the dog. "Not I," said the duck.

"Then I will do it myself," said the little red hen. And she did.

She took the wheat and made it into flour. Then she made warm, soft bread.

"Who will help me eat the bread?" she asked.

"I will!" said the cat. "I will!" said the dog. "I will!" said the duck.

"You did not help me work," said the hen. "But I will share with my chicks."

Her little chicks helped her every day. So they all ate the warm bread together and smiled.

title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf
content:
A little boy watched the sheep on a green hill.

The day was long, and the boy was bored.

"I will play a trick," he said. "Wolf! Wolf! A wolf is here!"

The town people ran up the hill to help him. But there was no wolf.

The boy laughed and laughed. The people were not happy.

The next day, the boy did it again. "Wolf! Wolf!" he cried.

The people ran up the hill. But there was no wolf. The boy just laughed.

The people walked home, slow and tired.

The boy thought about his trick. "That was not kind," he said. "I will tell the truth now."

From that day, the boy was honest. He kept the sheep safe and never told a lie again.

The people trusted him, and the boy felt warm and happy inside.

title: Stone Soup
content:
A kind traveler came to a small town. He was hungry and tired.

"Hello!" he said. "I will make stone soup. It is yummy!"

The people came to look. "Soup from a stone?" they said.

The traveler put a big pot of water on the fire. He dropped in a smooth, gray stone.

"This soup is good," he said. "But a carrot would make it better."

"I have a carrot!" said a girl. She put it in the pot.

"Now we need an onion," said the traveler.

"I have an onion!" said a boy. He put it in the pot.

One by one, the people brought potatoes, peas, and beans.

The soup smelled warm and sweet. "It is ready!" said the traveler.

Everyone sat down together. They ate the soup and laughed.

"When we share, we all have enough," said the traveler.

And the whole town had a happy, warm dinner.

title: The Ant and the Grasshopper
content:
In the warm summer, a grasshopper played all day.

He sang songs and jumped in the green grass.

A little ant walked by. She carried a big seed.

"Why do you work so hard?" said the grasshopper. "Come and play!"

"I am saving food for winter," said the ant. "Winter is cold."

"Winter is far away," laughed the grasshopper. And he played some more.

The ant worked every day. She carried seeds to her warm home.

Then the cold winter came. Snow fell soft and white.

The grasshopper had no food and no warm home. He was cold and sad.

He went to the ant's house and knocked on the door.

The kind ant opened the door. "Come in," she said. "I worked hard, so I have enough to share."

The grasshopper came in and ate warm food.

"Thank you," he said. "Next summer, I will work too."

And the ant and the grasshopper stayed warm together.

title: The Three Billy Goats Gruff
content:
Three billy goats lived on a brown, dry hill.

Across a little bridge was a green field full of soft, sweet grass.

The smallest goat went first. Trip, trap, trip, trap on the bridge.

"Who is on my bridge?" said a grumpy troll.

"It is only me," said the small goat. "My big brother is coming. He is much bigger."

"Go on then," said the troll.

The middle goat went next. Trip, trap, trip, trap.

"Who is on my bridge?" said the troll.

"My big brother is coming," said the middle goat. The troll let him pass.

The big goat went last. Trip, trap, trip, trap.

The troll saw the big goat's strong horns. "Oh my!" said the troll. He felt shy and ran away to nap by the river.

The three goats stood together on the green field.

"We helped each other," they said. And they ate sweet grass all day, happy and free.

title: The Kind Little Cloud
content:
High in the blue sky lived a small white cloud.

Every day, the little cloud floated over the hills.

One day, she looked down and saw a dry, brown field.

The flowers were thirsty. The little plants were sad.

"I can help," said the kind little cloud.

She took a big, deep breath. She grew bigger and gray.

Then the little cloud made soft rain. Pitter, patter, pitter, patter.

The rain fell on the field. The plants drank and drank.

Slowly, the brown field turned green. Little flowers opened up.

"Thank you, kind cloud!" said the happy flowers.

The little cloud felt light and white again. She smiled.

"It feels good to help," she said.

Every day, the little cloud helped the fields. And the world below was full of flowers.

title: Benny Bear Says Thank You
content:
Benny Bear lived in a cozy cave in the woods.

One morning, Benny was very hungry. He had no honey at all.

Benny went to see his friend, Bee.

"Hello, Bee," said Benny. "May I please have some honey?"

"Yes, you may," said Bee. She gave Benny a jar of sweet honey.

"Thank you so much!" said Benny with a big smile.

Next, Benny met Rabbit. Rabbit gave him a crunchy carrot.

"Thank you, Rabbit!" said Benny.

Then Squirrel gave Benny some nuts. "Thank you, Squirrel!" said Benny.

Benny went home with honey, a carrot, and nuts.

"My friends are so kind," said Benny. "I want to say thank you again."

The next day, Benny made a yummy picnic for all his friends.

"Thank you for being my friends," said Benny.

Bee, Rabbit, and Squirrel all hugged Benny. They had a happy day together.

title: The Brave Little Star
content:
Far up in the night sky lived a tiny little star.

All the big stars shone bright and gold.

"I am too small," said the little star. "My light is so tiny."

One dark night, a little girl could not sleep. Her room was very dark.

The girl looked out her window. "Please, little star," she said. "Help me see."

The little star felt shy. "My light is so small," she said. "But I will try."

The brave little star shone as bright as she could.

Her light came down, soft and warm, into the girl's room.

The girl smiled. "Thank you, little star! Now I am not afraid."

The girl closed her eyes and fell fast asleep.

The little star felt big and happy inside.

"Even a small light can help," she said.

And every night, the brave little star shone for all the sleepy children below.
